decisions.reason: Column named 'label' with two categories (yes/no), clear classification task.
alternatives_considered: No other plausible target columns - all other columns have high cardinality or numeric values.

decisions.choice: keep outliers; drop rows with no label; rarest class: keep; no columns excluded
decisions.reason: Missing values are minimal (0.01%). No columns appear to be identifiers. Rarest class 'yes' appears valid (7,464 samples, 24% of data). No obvious outliers to remove.
alternatives_considered: drop_rows_with_missing_label=false: would impute missing labels but imputing labels invents answers

decisions.reason: gradient_boosting: Shortlist leader with 0.7665 f1_macro, handles high-cardinality categoricals well, robust to heterogeneous features. logistic_regression: Second in shortlist (0.7649), complementary linear bias, interpretable coefficients, handles class imbalance through weighting.
alternatives_considered: random_forest: similar performance (0.7572) but more bias similarity with gradient_boosting
svm: 0.7587 but requires scaling and sensitive to kernel choice
svm: similar linear bias but more complex tuning
knn: 0.7469, distance-based but sensitive to high cardinality features

stopping.gradient_boosting: early stopping on validation loss with 10-round patience
stopping.logistic_regression: L-BFGS solver with default tol=1e-4 and max_iter=100

decisions.reason: gradient_boosting: not required - tree-based methods are scale-invariant logistic_regression: effectively required - linear models are sensitive to feature scales
alternatives_considered: gradient_boosting with scale=True - the registry's stated preference for this family is in reference.md section 3
logistic_regression with scale=False - the registry's stated preference for this family is in reference.md section 3

decisions.reason: Rows are independent (no detected entity groups). 5-fold stratified CV balances rare class representation (~1,493 'yes' per fold). K-fold provides stability for hyperparameter selection with imbalanced data.
alternatives_considered: holdout: simpler but single estimate less stable for rare class
3-fold: fewer folds but larger per-fold rare count (~2,488)

decisions.reason: Class imbalance (3.2:1 ratio) makes f1_macro more appropriate than accuracy.
alternatives_considered: precision: focuses on positive predictions but ignores recall

decisions.reason: Critical to balance precision and recall for minority class 'yes' in imbalanced dataset.
alternatives_considered: accuracy - Accuracy misleading with 76% majority class; could achieve 76% by always predicting 'no'.

decisions.decision: what the final model is fitted on
decisions.reason: With kfold validation, all non-test data is seen exactly once during validation, so using pool maximizes training data.
alternatives_considered: train - the scopes differ in how much data the final fit sees and, for 'pool', in whether the test estimate is still untouched by selection
train+validation - the scopes differ in how much data the final fit sees and, for 'pool', in whether the test estimate is still untouched by selection
